### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/index.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9cc5010c708c55d9a0d0c58d955e4b0293cef904` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6803dec38c237750374bc19e8181f2b6b8549f41` — the merge of head `52f0330d9781b1ef3e1dbdadfc78a68f47f35755` into base `9cc5010c708c55d9a0d0c58d955e4b0293cef904`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6803dec38c237750374bc19e8181f2b6b8549f41 && git checkout 6803dec38c237750374bc19e8181f2b6b8549f41
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9cc5010c708c55d9a0d0c58d955e4b0293cef904 52f0330d9781b1ef3e1dbdadfc78a68f47f35755 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9cc5010c708c55d9a0d0c58d955e4b0293cef904 && git merge --no-ff 52f0330d9781b1ef3e1dbdadfc78a68f47f35755

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9cc5010c708c55d9a0d0c58d955e4b0293cef904
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9cc5010c708c55d9a0d0c58d955e4b0293cef904` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

<sub>read 2026-09-21T20:42Z</sub>

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `52f0330d9781b1ef3e1dbdadfc78a68f47f35755`

### ① Derived judgments

Declared member, as it stands at this head:

`getEffectiveObjectPermissions?(context?: SecurityContext): Promise<Readonly<Record<string, EffectiveObjectPermission>>>`

**Is the declared shape RIGHT — the three anchors, each read from the tree rather than taken from the body.**

- **`EvalContext.permissions`.** `packages/formula/src/types.ts:120` declares it `EvalPermissions`; `:40` declares `EvalPermissions = Readonly<Record<string, EffectiveObjectPermission>>`, over `EffectiveObjectPermission` imported from `@objectstack/spec/security` (`:16`). The declared return is that construction verbatim, over the same element type. This is the ruling's own named target slot, so the engine half hands the answer straight in with no reshaping.
- **`GetEffectivePermissionsResponse.objects`.** `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:2569` — `z.record(z.string(), EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema)`. A `Record` is assignable into a `Readonly<Record>` return, so the endpoint's map flows through unchanged. `readonly` on a return position constrains the caller, not the implementer, so it is the safe direction and not a narrowing.
- **`EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema`.** `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts:595`, type at `:617` (`z.input<…>`). Confirmed **not** declared in `protocol.zod.ts`, which only imports it at `:28` — the seat's corrected reading is the right one.

**Parameter, optionality, and the absent context.** `context?: SecurityContext` is character-for-character the sibling spelling at `security-service.ts:397` (`resolvePermissionSetsForContext?(context?: SecurityContext)`), and `SecurityContext = Partial<ExecutionContext>` is all-optional by construction with the type's own docblock covering partial callers. An absent context therefore needs no separate clause on this member, and the answer it yields — an empty map — is already a defined real answer under the member's own doc rather than an undefined state. No gap, and the optional `?` is what a widening requires.

**The three shape questions really are closed by published contracts; I read the closures, not the argument for them.** `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts:160-162` states that "an object the effective map does not mention is an object with no grant, and answers `false`" — so a caller may not narrow the map, and the reader correctly takes no object parameter. `stdlib.ts:198-207` is the failure stance in the consumer's own runtime code: with `binding.permissions === undefined`, `can()` throws, and its message names the shape outright — "the `objects` map of the published /auth/me/permissions response, object name -> EffectiveObjectPermission". No map is a loud throw, an empty map is a quiet real answer, so a reader that degraded to `{}` would publish a denial of everything as measured fact. The declared contract matches on all three.

**Was the published type reused rather than duplicated? Yes.** `EffectiveObjectPermission` is imported from `../security/permission.zod.js`; no parallel entry shape is declared anywhere in the diff. The only thing restated is the `Readonly<Record<string, …>>` wrapper, and it **must** be restated: `packages/spec/package.json` carries no `@objectstack/formula` dependency in `dependencies`, `devDependencies` or `peerDependencies`, while `packages/formula/package.json` depends on `@objectstack/spec` (`workspace:*`). Importing `EvalPermissions` would invert that direction, so restating the wrapper over the imported element type is the only available spelling. Not a duplicate shape.

**The census question — `done` is the right call, and `needs_decision` would have been wrong.** The ground is the ruling text, not the author's argument for it. Comment `5725678115` does not merely order a census. Under **Interface** it directs: 「the claimant files the spec sub-card for the member (`Clause-②: yes`, the spec lane's at-tier review, changeset `@objectstack/spec` minor) and this card carries the wiring (`packages/objectql` + `packages/plugins/plugin-security`), `Blocked-by:` that sub-card」. The ruling pre-specified this PR's clause, its review tier, its semver level **and** its shape (「the caller's effective object permissions in the `/auth/me/permissions` shape (the map `can` already reads)」). The **Census first** bullet defines its own rows as "populates `permissions`, or is out of scope with a reason" — rows about evaluation SITES, carried by the wiring card. The board agrees: #19578 is titled as the `packages/spec` half and #18783 is `pm:blocked` / `domain:engine`, so the split is recorded rather than asserted. A census over sites cannot move a return type pinned at both ends by already-published contracts, and the body declares 「⛔ No census was run here」 outright rather than implying one. The contract was not declared prematurely.

**Do the pins pin the contract, or merely the syntax? Mostly the contract.**

- The `@ts-expect-error` on the unguarded call pins OPTIONALITY, and it is self-falsifying: `security-service.test.ts` has no entry in `packages/spec/test-typecheck-debt.json` (53 entries, none matching; control — `src/ai/conversation.test.ts` is one of them), so its budget is zero and an unused directive reds `check:test-typecheck`.
- Optionality is closed from the other direction too, by the file's pre-existing `RequiredMember` / `UnlistedRequiredMember` / `satisfies readonly RequiredMember[]` machinery: making the member required would make `UnlistedRequiredMember` non-empty and stop the file compiling.
- The RETURN TYPE is genuinely pinned, because `makeService(overrides: Partial<ISecurityService>)` type-checks every override literal against the declared signature. `apiOperations: ['get', 'list']` is the real discriminator: `apiOperations` exists only on the response-side `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema` and deliberately **not** on the authoring `ObjectPermissionSchema`, and both values are members of `API_OPERATION_ORDER` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:65`). Swapping the element type to the authoring one would fail excess-property checking, so the test pins the effective-vs-authored distinction it claims to pin.

⚠️ **Two nits, neither a FAIL ground.** (a) The body states "the three `@ts-expect-error` pins"; this diff adds **one**. The file carries 7 at this head, 6 of them pre-existing. The mechanism the sentence relies on is sound, but the count is wrong and a reader checking the claim will not find three. (b) Two of the five new assertions measure language semantics rather than the contract: `expect(withoutIt.getEffectiveObjectPermissions?.({…})).toBeUndefined()` holds by optional chaining alone, and `expect(map && 'lead' in map).toBe(false)` / `expect(map?.lead).toBeUndefined()` assert about a literal the test itself wrote. The normative "absent entry = no grant" rule is enforced in `@objectstack/formula`, which `packages/spec` cannot reach from here — so those lines document rather than pin.

**`api-surface` / `json-schema` untouched is CORRECT — verified with a radius and a control, not accepted.** `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json` records `ISecurityService (interface)`: an export NAME plus kind. `getReadableFields`, a pre-existing MEMBER of that same interface, appears in **no** api-surface shard (exit 1), while `ISecurityService` appears in the same radius (exit 0) — so interface members are not recorded, and adding one moves nothing. `api-surface-signatures.json` is scoped to the 27 `defineX` factories (read in full); `ISecurityService` is not one, and `build-api-surface.ts`'s own SCOPE docblock confirms both artifacts describe the export surface only. In `packages/spec/json-schema/`, `ISecurityService` is absent (exit 1) while `EffectiveObjectPermission` is present (exit 0 — `json-schema/security/EffectiveObjectPermission.json` and `objectstack.json`): the radius is zod schemas, and a TypeScript interface member falls outside it. No regeneration was owed, and no baseline update is missing.

### ② Semver level

The changeset grades `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, and `@objectstack/spec` is the only package this diff moves. Against `judgeLevel` (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:1618`) that yields `offenders` (moved packages graded `patch`) empty and `raised` (moved packages graded `minor` or above) = `@objectstack/spec minor`, so `refusable = offenders.length > 0 && raised.length === 0` is **false**: the level axis discharges rather than reaching the `enforce` verdict. `minor` is correct and required for a widening, and no other moved package is left at `patch` because there is no other moved package. `Check Changeset` is green on both of its runs.

### ③ Boundary flags

**`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is correct, judged from the diff and the card.** The source file's entire change is one optional member added to `ISecurityService`, plus the single deleted line — the existing type-only import, rewritten to add `EffectiveObjectPermission` to its brace list. Nothing renamed, nothing narrowed, nothing removed; a security service that omits the member still satisfies the contract. Declared in both the PR body and the changeset.

**Scope discipline holds.** 3 files, `+216/−1`: the changeset, `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.test.ts`. Nothing under `packages/objectql`, nothing in `plugin-security`, nothing touching `evaluateOptionVisibility` — the engine half stays with #18783, which is `pm:blocked` on this card.

⚠️ **CI state at review time: NOT CONVERGED — and this verdict does not underwrite the part that had not landed.** At the reading stamped above, the head carried 37 check runs: **27 `success`, 6 `skipped`, 4 still `in_progress`** — `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`. **Zero** were red, failed, cancelled or timed out, and none turned red while I watched the set converge from 14 outstanding down to 4. Everything this review's own findings rest on had already landed green: `Lint & Repo Gates` (which settles the line-length question the new import line raises), `Build Core`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Check Changeset` on both runs, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` on all three shards, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, and `Test Core` shards 2/6, 3/6 and 4/6.

⛔ But `Test Core` is one of the seven `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` (`scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs`), so three of its six shards plus the workspace typecheck were still outstanding when this record was written. The verdict below is the **contract** verdict — the shape, the reuse, the census call, the clause, the level, the scope, the pins and the baselines — and it does **not** attest to those four runs. Confirm they are green before acting on it; anything red there is a finding this record has not made.

**Not acted on by this review.** `needs:contract-review` is left hanging as dispatched; no label write, push, approval, draft flip, enqueue or merge was performed. The docs-drift comment is advisory and its gate is green — neither page it lists enumerates `ISecurityService` members (`content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx:42` is a one-line prose row), so this member leaves no doc obligation behind. #18545, named on the card's Refs line, answers 404; per dispatch that is a suspended account's issue and nothing was inferred from its absence.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19578-isecurityservice-effective-object-permission-reader`
Reviewed-by: `session_01AmH9bKvGoLjiY86Q4Z3og2`

**VERDICT: PASS**
